feature_title: EPI/WGI bronze ingestion via Dataflow Gen2 (EPI_file2table, WGI_file2table)
rationale: The last two Dataflow Gen2 items in the workspace, both orphaned since task-035 repointed the orchestrator to notebooks on 2026-07-26. Their replacements are strictly better: EPI_file2table read a hand-uploaded CSV from the lakehouse Files/ area, whereas bronze_ingest_epi downloads epi{year}results.csv straight from epi.yale.edu with retry and year-parameterisation (and additionally produces bronze_epi2024weights, which the dataflow never did); WGI_file2table read a hand-uploaded Excel extract carrying only 2023 percentile ranks in 4 columns, whereas bronze_ingest_wgi pulls all 6 WGI indicators for 1996-2023 in long format from the World Bank API. Both notebooks say so in their own headers ('Replaces manual CSV upload via ..._file2table.Dataflow'). Retired now rather than left in place because they were not inert: .github/workflows/deploy-fabric.yml lists 'Dataflow' in item_type_in_scope, so fabric-cicd republished both on every deploy, and every publish strips Dataflow Gen2 credentials (they live outside the git definition) - the entire KNOWN LIMITATION block in fabric/parameter.yml existed solely to service these two dead items. Measured on 2026-08-10 before removal: the live pipeline had 10 activities and zero RefreshDataflow; every job-history entry for both dataflows was invokeType=Manual, i.e. the orchestrator never triggered them; last manual runs were 2026-07-26 (EPI) and 2026-07-25 (WGI). Decommissioning them was originally scoped under task-005 and never carried out; task-035 closed with 'EPI_file2table is now orphaned (nothing invokes it) and was left in place', and task-046/task-049 both flagged the leftover. Retirement mechanism chosen by Erik 2026-08-10, following the bronze-azuresqldb2table-dataflow precedent.
restore_notes:
READ THIS BEFORE RESTORING.

0. WHY YOU PROBABLY SHOULD NOT RESTORE THESE. They are strictly weaker than the notebooks that replaced them, and they reintroduce a manual-upload step plus a credential that every CI publish strips. The only sane reason to restore is to demonstrate a Dataflow Gen2 artifact for its own sake - in which case build a fresh one rather than reviving these.

1. COMMIT PIN. commit_sha is the last commit where both dataflows were live in main (HEAD immediately before the retirement commit), per rules/feature-retirement.md Step 2. Cherry-pick or copy from this SHA.

2. DOUBLE-WRITER HAZARD - THE BIG ONE. Both dataflows write the SAME lakehouse tables the live notebooks now write: EPI_file2table -> bronze_epi2024results (= bronze_ingest_epi's target) and WGI_file2table -> bronze_WGI, which is the SAME TABLE as the notebook's bronze_wgi because the metastore lowercases identifiers. Restoring without also removing/disabling the bronze_epi and bronze_wgi TridentNotebook activities gives you two writers on one table and last-writer-wins, silently, with no error. Decide which side owns each table BEFORE restoring.

3. THE WGI SCHEMAS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. The dataflow emitted 4 columns (Country Name, Country Code, Series Name, Percentile Rank 2023) for 2023 only, on a 0-100 percentile scale. The notebook emits long format, all 6 indicators, 1996-2023, on the World Bank ESTIMATE scale (approx -2.5..+2.5). spec_v1.md line 435 documents that no 0-100 range rule is enforced on silver_wgi precisely because of this. Swapping the producer back changes the value domain and will silently invalidate any downstream range assumption. Check bronze_to_silver's WGI branch before flipping the producer.

4. APPLICATION STATE IS NOT IN THE SNAPSHOT AND WAS PROBABLY DELETED. Both dataflows read hand-uploaded files from the oem_lh lakehouse Files/ area (488fb9f8-e635-4683-90c4-ba4fee9dfadb, workspace 99e4cc6d-6ec3-49a7-aed9-b69b04a97aa9): Files/EPI/epi2024results.csv and Files/WGI/P_Data_Extract_From_Worldwide_Governance_Indicators.xlsx. Those are data, not code, so they are deliberately NOT in the snapshot. Verify they still exist before expecting a refresh to succeed; if not, re-download from epi.yale.edu and the World Bank databank respectively.

5. GEN2 CREDENTIAL RE-BINDING. Both are Dataflow Gen2, so every fabric-cicd publish leaves them deployed-but-unbound; the credential lives INSIDE the dataflow definition, not in Settings -> Manage connections and gateways. fabric/parameter.yml carried a KNOWN LIMITATION block covering exactly this, narrowed to these two items after the Azure SQL dataflow retirement and removed entirely at this retirement. Restore that guidance alongside the items.

6. DEPLOY SCOPE. .github/workflows/deploy-fabric.yml had 'Dataflow' removed from item_type_in_scope at retirement. Re-add it or fabric-cicd will not publish the restored items at all.

7. STAGING ARTIFACTS WERE DELETED TOO. StagingLakehouseForDataflows_20250822093021, its SQL endpoint, and StagingWarehouseForDataflows_20250822093045 were removed in the same pass; all three held zero tables. Fabric auto-recreates staging artifacts when a Gen2 dataflow with staging is created, so this needs no manual restore - but expect new items with new timestamped names to appear. EPI_file2table declares StagingDefinition = [Kind = 'FastCopy'].

8. SPEC MARKERS TO REVERT. spec_v1.md carries Retired (2026-08-10) markers added via /iterate per DEC-016 - do NOT edit the spec inline. Locations at retirement: ~210 (EPI ingestion method), ~257/263 (WGI file format + ingestion method), ~435 (WGI range-rule rationale), ~1012-1018 (Naming Conventions / Dataflows), ~1038 (consistency notes), ~1485 (appendix EPI source note).

9. UNMARKED MIRROR DOCS. README.md, docs/architecture/fabric-artifacts-inventory.md, docs/architecture/fabric_workspace.md, docs/architecture/data_sources.md, docs/architecture/medallion_architecture.md, docs/epi_wgi_ingestion.md, .claude/commands/run-bronze.md and .claude/commands/run-silver.md all describe these items. They sit outside the spec, take no retirement marker, and were updated at retirement - check them on restore.

10. NO CREDENTIALS ARE INVOLVED. Unlike bronze-azuresqldb2table-dataflow, both sources are public (Yale EPI over HTTPS, World Bank databank export). There is no secret to recover.
